We called the guesses a "hypothesis" to make it a little more scientific sounding. It is fun for the whole family. It says you need 2 players, but my 6 year old likes to play alone. Educational Insights Design & Drill All Aboard Train, 30 Piece Take Apart Toy with Electric Drill Toy, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 3+ [[VIDEOID:979dc2c95d283020e887dc97f4539982]] There is supposed to be a motorized drill included with this set, but only the drill socket was included. Happily, the conductor has a hole on the bottom that can be used to tighten or loosen the bolts. My three-year-old niece was content with using this as is and loves the train so much as a toy that I'll give it 3 stars, but I think many children would prefer the fun of the motorized drill. When you press a button, the train makes a chu-chu sound and a very dim white light comes out the front. You can't see the light unless you're looking for it. The "design and drill" is basically some bolts to screw on to hold the covers and the wheels in place. There were several colors of bolts you can choose from to make different "designs."

The engine measures 10 inches long by 6 inches wide by 6 inches tall. The wagon measures 7.5 inches long by 6 inches wide by 3.75 inches tall. The wagon bed is 2 inches deep. The caboose measures 7.5 inches long 6 inches wide and 5 inches tall. Three AAA batteries are needed to power the drill according to the instruction manual, and two AAA batteries are needed for the train engine for the sound and light. The wheels roll smoothly and securely, and it is easy to connect the three sections of the train together, so it is a good toy not just a building activity. There are some extra bolts in case some are lost. The train is sturdy and can withstand the rough treatment of a 3-year-old armed with a plastic hammer.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Design & Drill All Aboard Train, 30 Piece Take Apart Toy with Electric Drill Toy, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 3+

hand2mind 20 Bead Wooden Rekenrek Activity Set, Abacus for Kids Math, Math Manipulatives Kindergarten, Counting Rack for Kids, Counters for Kids Math, Educational Toys for Elementary Kids (Set of 1) This ETA HAND2MIND 20-BEAD REKENREK (with Activity Guide) is a solid, beautifully made wood-and-metal counting frame. The beads feel nice, and slide easily. The frame is accompanied by a teaching manual that includes lessons, number “cards” to be cut out and mounted on heavier stock, and student problem worksheets for duplication.

The Rekenrek is intended to help students visualize numbers. I found the lessons hard to follow at first—an important element is understanding that the starting “Home” position is with all the beads on the right. If taught correctly, I can see how the Rekenrek would make early math classes (K-2) more tactile and fun.

The Rekenrek isn’t expensive (about $15 on Amazon), considering how well-made it is. However, it will cost a fair amount to equip a class for “Rekenrek math”. One Rekenrek is required for each student, and one for the teacher.
text_fidelity_b: hand2mind 20 Bead Wooden Rekenrek Activity Set, Abacus for Kids Math, Math Manipulatives Kindergarten, Counting Rack for Kids, Counters for Kids Math, Educational Toys for Elementary Kids (Set of 1)

text_fidelity_a:
Schleich Dinosaurs, Realistic Large Dinosaur Toys for Boys and Girls, Barapasaurus Toy Figurine, Ages 4+ As usual with Schleich toys, you can’t fault the durability or the quality. I’ve reviewed a number of them, and I can’t speak highly enough of their quality builds. They are made to last, even if roughly played with. We’ve had several now for about a decade, and they look no different than when they arrived, despite having gone through a number of dino “battles” and the like. This one is no exception. One issue I suppose is that it may be a little over-built in that it has quite a heft to it, which may preclude younger children from playing easily with it. It’s sizable already, but add the weight and I can see small hands having a difficult time picking it up and moving it around, or certainly moving it smoothly. Once you move past the toddler years, though, that will be much less of an issue.

In terms of looks, it’s nicely painted (again, as usual with Schleich), with the blue cuts running down central area from head to tail tip standing out particularly nicely. The pose is as if it is about to take a step forward or perhaps step on something (someone?). The face is my one real complaint about this model. It’s a raw sort of red color, which isn’t all that aesthetic. It almost looks like it’s been flayed, or perhaps is furiously angry. And there’s something about the mouth being open in the manner it is that just seems a bit off-putting.But at least the teeth look like the right sort (I hate when one has, for instance, obviously carnivorous teeth on herbivores).

It’s nice to have a new model and a relatively unknown one at that. Outside of the head/face, which is a relatively minor complaint, the barapasuaruk is another fine addition to a great line of toys/models.
text_fidelity_b: Schleich Dinosaurs, Realistic Large Dinosaur Toys for Boys and Girls, Barapasaurus Toy Figurine, Ages 4+

text_fidelity_a:
YEHUONU 19 pcs Diamond Painting Stickers Kits, Mosaic Sticker Art Kits Superhero Princess Patterns ,for Men Women Kids Boys Girls This diamond painting kit from YEHUONU is great for kids and adults. I was curious about diamond painting but didn’t want to commit to a big one, I didn’t know if I’d like it or not. This kit has 19 different princesses and superheroes to do, measuring about 2 to 3.5 inches tall and about 2 to 3 inches wide. So the figures are relatively small, about an hour’s worth of time to complete, depending on age and speed.

The back of the box includes basic instructions. This was my first time, so I also watched a video to better understand how to use the wax block (the box calls it “solid glue” which is an interesting translation).

The diamonds do not come in resealable baggies, which is a negative. The same colors are used from character to character. For example, many of the princesses use the same bright yellow for their hair. But if I do one princess today and another in the future, I have to put those yellow diamonds in a new baggie to store inbetween.

The baggies come in a long strip with perforations to tear them free -- be careful. In my experience, the baggies tore when I tried to separate them, so I cut them apart.

The different images can be cut apart. I recommend this, since you don’t want to remove the top plastic until you’re ready to paint with diamonds (the canvases are sticky underneath the plastic). Some of the princesses are very close together which does make cutting them apart a little tricky.
text_fidelity_b: YEHUONU 19 pcs Diamond Painting Stickers Kits, Mosaic Sticker Art Kits Superhero Princess Patterns ,for Men Women Kids Boys Girls

Colored Pencil Set with Case, 7-Inch, Pack of 72 As an artist, I like to keep a variety of pencils on hand for different projects. I decided to test these out in an adult coloring book (with a fairy) and I am actually very impressed. I had low expectations, a lot of people seem to dislike them, but personally I really like them. My husband works at an art and craft store so I have tried a lot of brands and styles. This pack is a great one for starters or to add to your color palette in pencils. Colored pencils can be blended, but it's a lot easier to have a variety of colors to get the shade you want. I spent about 2 hours coloring this page using only pencils from this pack. There are a few colors I would like to have seen, but over all it's still a very diverse pack. There are a lot of lighter and brighter tons than I have in my other pencils.

The pencils themselves have not given me any trouble. The wood is a little lighter than say the Crayola brand ones, but they sharpen fine and as long as you aren't pressing extremely hard the lead does not break. I pressed fairly hard to blend the trees and none of the pencils broke for me. While this was not an art venture, this page was used for me to test the pencils and I am happy with the results. Before I would color on the page, I used a blank page to scribble a little as it can be hard to differentiate some of the colors from the other shades, but I do this anyway so I am sure about the color I want before I get it on the page and accidentally wreck something.

The colors blended fine, I probably should have gone back and finished shading, but as a test page it worked fine. I mixed this pack in with my other pencils so I can choose from any color I could need. When I started out I used the cheap brand from the craft store and these are much higher quality than those ever were.

I wouldn't consider the plastic thing a case though, it's more like a package. Not easy to use. I put my pencils in a storage tote so I could easily go through and choose the one I need. I may end up buying another pack for my mother down the road, she likes to color and basic pencil sets do not have this variety of colors. The price is extremely competitive as well. I paid almost this much for my set of 48 Crayola pencils.

*I RECEIVED THIS PRODUCT (IN ORDER TO TRY IT AND REVIEW) THIS DOES NOT GUARANTEE A GOOD REVIEW OR CHANGE MY OPINION ON THE PRODUCT, I AM HONEST AND UNBIASED, ALL OPINIONS ON IT ARE MY OWN AND BASED ON THE PRODUCT ITSELF. I HAVE TRIED THIS MYSELF AND EVALUATED IT ACCORDINGLY

Evviva Ant Habitat W/LED Light. Enjoy A Magnificent Habitat. Great for Kids & Adults. Evviva Ant Ecosystem W/Enhanced Blue Gel. Educational & Learning Science Kit. Live Ants Not Included This ant farm was a fascinating gift for everyone, not just the 6 year old who got it. We ordered the ants from AntsAlive .com and when they arrived they quickly scurried about, digging their first hole within a few hours. Before you add the ants, you must poke 3 to 4 holes in the gel to help the ants get started. I’m wondering if the negative reviews forgot this step, leaving the ants confused in the farm on where they could go.

I highly recommend refrigerating the ants for 10 minutes before you add them to the farm so they don’t immediately escape. I also highly recommend putting them in on the side nearest the white air hole plug. Inevitably a few ants will have died in shipment and it’s much easier to remove them through the hole then removing the entire lid (as others will try to escape).

Why this ant farm is better than others?
1) The ants food and water supply is in the gel. Other ant farms require food and water be added for the ants; adding too much can create mold or too little and the ants are hungry. It’s challenging to calculate and extra work.

2) The glass is fairly narrow front to back so it’s likely the ants (as they did for us) will dig right to the class so you can see them clearly while they work under ground.

3) The light and magnifying glass make it very easy to see every ant at work.

4) The farm is reusable. You can clean out the old gel and ants and buy new ants and gel for a second use.

I highly recommend this gift for any child aged 4-10. Certainly older children and adults will enjoy it too.

*The attached photos are of the ant farm on day 3.

Giant Clue Classic Mystery Party Retro Board Game Summer Toy with Large Rooms, Giant Cards, and Foam Tools, for Kids and Families Ages 8 and up We tried this recently on a rainy evening, and it was a fun family activity. However it feels like some things weren't fully thought through and could have been easily made better.
For example, the spinner needle feels like it stops exactly on the line more than half the time, causing much arguing and debate over which side it actually landed. If you have ever played the game Life or used a spinning prize wheel, you know there is a much better way to do this: Have plastic borders that catch on the needle so it stops in one space clearly (and makes a cool motor noise as it click-click-clicks quickly). Once you're making giant playing pieces and a large floor mat board, this would not have added a lot of cost and would have made the game infinitely more fun and smooth to play.
And speaking of giant playing pieces, once you assemble them, they don't fit back in the box unless you break them apart, something that probably won't last if you do it every time you put the game away. It could have come with a bag or something to store the game board and pieces in. As of now, I'm pretty sure the pieces and board are going to get separated from each other in our family room. It's a fun game, but unlike giant versions of Jenga, Connect Four or Chess, the novelty of giant Sorry wears off quickly and at some point my mother-in-law actually asked why we can't just play it on the table like a regular game. It's fun for the novelty, but the caveats and game mechanics make this not worth more than 3 stars in my opinion.
text_fidelity_b: Giant Clue Classic Mystery Party Retro Board Game Summer Toy with Large Rooms, Giant Cards, and Foam Tools, for Kids and Families Ages 8 and up

In water when you wiggle the tale, the fin sort of sparkles and has that color changing effect. The plastic tail by itself does not change at all. da Vinci's Room Awkward Turtle The Word Party Card Game with a Dirty Sense of Humor for Groups of 4 or More People Gave this as a gift to a recipient out of state- Due to that fact, I never felt capable of reviewing the product. Craziest thing… almost a year later, when we went On vacation and met up for dinner at the house I sent this too..(can you follow that..?!) to my happy surprise- they were all playing awkward turtles!! Yep, the game I had sent to them almost a year prior!! (could have been contrived Sure-but, from the wear and tear on the game… I knew they had been using it all along.)

Of course, we went to have Dinner with the adults at the house.. But, their group of teen/20+ yr olds were laughing hysterically in the other room having “game night“ and I promise, they were having way more fun than we were!!

I peaked in on the gameplaying and the concept looked pretty straightforward. Basically, divided into two teams… One member has an awkward word and tries to describe it to their team- if guessed correctly they get points! And the game sort of back-and-forths from there… Funny, quirky, annoying, cringe worthy, racy words all make up the options.. These kids were playing the game when we arrived- 2hr. Later we left... And they were still playing! (No! Not the same round but, plenty of rounds and all entertained long enough to still be having fun hours later.)

To me, this is the best type of endorsement one can have… Seeing a game in action and hearing the laughter as it was being played. This told me all I needed to know… The game was a hit for the crowd at hand- it kept them happily playing for hours. Combined it with the ease of which it takes to “learn” the game.. And you’ve got a winner in my book!

LEGO Creator Expert 10253 Big Ben Building Kit As will become clear in this review, I am a true fan of Lego. Does that bias my review? I dont think so, you may disagree...

This is a big set. This is not a set for your younger Lego builders, not because its too hard, but because some of it will become tedious to younger minds. But us older people refusing to grow up (46 and still building with Lego!) will love this. There are several points during the build where you think "Oh WOW, thats clever" - very good.
The end result is bigger than I expected. Most of my recent large set builds have been the modular Lego City sets, which are built the right size for Lego Minifigs - this is much smaller than that! So you cannot add it to your Lego City, but you can have it in the back ground.

Its about an 8 hour build. The manual is excellent, but with less writing than some of the other ones - the Lego Eiffel Tower's Manual had a lot more information on the history of the Tower. This has a few snippets about the history, the Big Ben bell, but more would have been appreciated.

When finished, it is beautiful. You can turn the knob on the back to adjust the time - you cannot really adjust the time - the hour and minute hand are tuck, so as one turns, so does the other. But its still awesome!
The tree outside the main entrance is wonderful! one of my favorite parts of the build!

I believe that Lego is the best toy ever made. This set only re-enforces that opinion. Some Legos, when complete can be played with (the Lego City ones, for instance) but others not so much. I dont see this being played with, just built, displayed, and maybe dismantled and rebuilt.

5 stars though. A wonderful Lego set. A must have for collectors big kids, and us huge kids!
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Creator Expert 10253 Big Ben Building Kit

Globe 540 Piece 3D Puzzle Ball Most puzzle balls come with the last five pieces pre-assembled. You have to sort of ease them/roll them into place--putting the last piece in by itself is close to impossible--and it can be quite a pain. Not this one.

This one has tiny holes on the top and bottom for stoppers that allow the puzzle to sit in the stand and turn (the thing spins smoothly, just like any good globe should). For some reason that makes putting the last piece, as a singleton piece, in easily. I just popped it in, with no more difficulty than putting in any other piece. That makes this a top choice for anyone just starting out with puzzle balls. You can assemble by image or by number. The pieces interlock smoothly and easily and hold together substantially better than most puzzle balls. It didn't fall apart a single time as I was working on it, even when adding a piece into a hole that has been built up around substantially. As a puzzle, this is orders of magnitude better than any puzzle ball I have ever assembled. It took just under two hours from start to finish, making it the fastest assembly for me, and I think I picked up a little geography as I went (my worst subject when I was in school).

The detailing on the countries is excellent. The print is clear. This can serve an an excelling globe after the puzzle is done. The stand is very nice too.

Highly, highly, highly recommend, especially for kids.
text_fidelity_b: Globe 540 Piece 3D Puzzle Ball

text_fidelity_a:
YIGO - Fun & Challenging Word Game for Clever Minds - Exciting Brain Game for Kids, Teens & Adults - Improves Spelling, Vocabulary & Memory - Educational Family Card Game for Boys & Girls [[VIDEOID:258489d4261f7a5b0f26535ccf27c4f9]] The plusses: The game is beautiful to look at and feels good quality. The print quality is very very good, these cards do not feel cheap, they feel almost like fancy plastic. It’s also a standard size which means if you are heavy users it’s not challenging to find sleeves to accommodate. I’m also pretty sure the box is big enough to handle sleeves. The rules are relatively simple, and the instruction manual provides a QR code that leads to a video of the gameplay combined with errata to the rules as written. You will *need* the errata because the rules do not answer very basic questions. It makes me wonder how much this was play-tested with strangers before release. It’s great to see a company offering solid support after release though!

At more than 100 cards, the deck is very unwieldy to shuffle, this is definitely one that needs to be broken into smaller piles to handle and then combined.

The rounds are much shorter than expected, some rounds were over in a 2 player game in as little as three fast turns. The actual gameplay is not one “game” but to have the least points over the series of many rounds (the most “loses” the game night.) There was very little tension or any emotional investment because of the fast turnover–that might work for some folks but it didn’t feel like it was worth working on big words without stalling. There were two rounds where the game was over in two turns before my husband could even play a card. It feels like more luck than skill which is not desirable in a word game. My biggest criticism is that due to the number of repeated vowels, gameplay can feel repetitive, we started round after round with “e” or “a” despite shuffling many times. I would love to see a second deck of a different color with starting letters distributed in a more logical way because the starting letter affects the gameplay variety over time. My husband and I love wordplay and puns as a rule and this game was not skill-based enough for the two-player version for us to want to invest too much more time on it. Maybe if we played it for longer there would be more to it but we both got bored after playing 10 or so rounds and probably wouldn’t give it a second try.

The idea itself is an awesome one, when it works it’s like combining scrabble with Uno. There is solid product quality and marketing. It just lacked the skill vs luck factor for us, which may be personal taste

I really think this game needs some tweaks to the gameplay to make it better before I’d really recommend it, at least on the game shelf of a couple. It says ages 8 and up, but I can’t imagine playing this with my almost 8yo, especially without eliminating some of the rules regarding “made up words” because 50 points penalty is pretty punitive for what might be an accidental misspelling, and even with some coaching it would be pretty difficult (And my kiddo has an above-average vocabulary). Maybe several 8yo together do well? We may try to break it out at a party among adults in the future.
text_fidelity_b: YIGO - Fun & Challenging Word Game for Clever Minds - Exciting Brain Game for Kids, Teens & Adults - Improves Spelling, Vocabulary & Memory - Educational Family Card Game for Boys & Girls

text_fidelity_a:
Boom Boom Balloon, Exciting Anticipation Family Board Game Outdoor Summer Toy, for Kids Ages 8 and up My oldest son(5) recently started daily injections. As you would expect, he hates them. We try to do something fun after each of them, and this was used as one of his "surprises". It did the trick and took his mind off that mean needle.

This game is really fun! Not only did my children enjoy it, but I did, too. It does come with a few issues, though.

First of all, as I put the thing together, the instructions say to never use your mouth to blow up the balloon. You must use a balloon pump. A balloon pump isn't included, so I chose to use my mouth to blow up the balloon, since I had excited children waiting to play. It went fine. I was able to blow up the balloon while it was in the frame without any problem.

Secondly, we couldn't get the top clip piece to stay put. There's a clip that holds the 3 pieces of the frame together at the top. It kept coming lose no matter how tight I tried to get it. When I took the thing apart, I couldn't get one frame piece to come apart. So, 2 were so lose the whole thing kept coming apart, but one was so tight I had to put it in the box together, and therefore, couldn't close the lid.

Third, one of the sticks was broke within minutes of playing the game. Thankfully, there are 4 extras included, so we can still play. Plus, the recommended age is 8 and up. I played this game with my 2 and 5 year olds. The 2 year old is the one that broke the stick, so I'm not taking stars off for that issue or anything. It's simply to warn you that they do break pretty easily.

There are 12 balloons included. They are all the same: blue, with a face. They are the regular sized balloons, so I imagine this game will work perfectly fine with store bought replacement balloons. You just probably won't have a face on there.

I know it sounds like a lot of complaining up there, but we really enjoyed this game!

The basics: You put the thing together, which is really simple. You put the balloon in the frame, blow it up, and then wrap it around the "hook" at the bottom to keep the air in without having to actually tie it. Super simple. You take the sticks and put them in the holes(6) until you hear the first click. Then you take turns rolling dice. Whatever number it lands on is the amount of times you push in a stick. It can be the same stick or one click each on different sticks. Whoever pops the balloon first loses(or wins if you're my children).

Overall, it's a fun game that's worth the issues that come with it.
text_fidelity_b: Boom Boom Balloon, Exciting Anticipation Family Board Game Outdoor Summer Toy, for Kids Ages 8 and up

My favorite feature is the bomb hatch located behind the pilot/passenger compartment that seats the minifigs. You can seat Spidey in the hatch, press a button, and let him drop down on his web string to dangle beneath the plane. You can also use the hatch to drop brick-built energy bombs. Behind the hatch, there is another compartment that opens for storing bombs and weapons.

The two little drones are quick to build. The drones and the Stark jet are all equipped with stud shooters. (Stud shooters are special spring-loaded bricks that shoot off single studs that were loaded onto them, when you move a lever.)

The jet has a minimum of stickers (always a good thing, in my opinion). The “adjustable wings” are the two upper ones at the tail. They can be adjusted to different angles. The big wings at the sides, and their wingtips, are fixed in place.

The kit includes minifigs for Happy Hogan, Nick Fury, Spider-Man, and Mysterio, as well as their associated weapons.

text_fidelity_a: Barbie Dreamtopia Sweetville Kingdom Carriage I have been a Barbie fan since I was a child, many years ago. My now 16 year old daughter was a huge fan when she was young. I even have several "in the box" collector Barbies. The Barbie Dreamtopia Sweetville Kingdom Carriage just doesn't seem as high quality as the many Barbie products I have purchased over the years. It's definitely not a collector's item. The price is decent and you get a complete set of a doll, unicorn, and carriage. The plastic carriage flexes when you apply pressure. It doesn't feel like it's going to easily break, but it's not as rigid as other Barbie products. The carriage door opens and closes.  The wheels rotate easily and give a pretty smooth ride. The details on the carriage are nice. There are lots of textures to make it more realistic.  The unicorn is a sturdier plastic piece. The doll has the rigid, no bend legs. Her facial details are what you expect on Barbies. She has a removable crown. Her top is molded plastic and not removable. Her skirt is a cute, candy print fabric, but the material itself is stiff and doesn't flow or move. In fact, I don't like the skirt at all. Overall, it's an attractive looking set, but the quality is disappointing. With all that said, I think young Barbie fans would probably still enjoy it.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Dreamtopia Sweetville Kingdom Carriage

The battery does say it will need 3 hours to charge though so BE READY to get that second battery on the charger right when you get this car.

Alex Art Wooden Dough Tools Set Kids Art and Craft Activity What you see is what you get! This fun set of clay manipulation tools would make a perfect gift alongside either play doh or one of the more sophisticated and fluffier types of modeling clay such as[[ASIN:B011TRQ3TO Sago Brothers 36 Colors Ultra Light Modeling Magic Air Dry Clay Crafts Kit]].

I think my favorites are the three rolling wheels, which are suited to small hands and fun to use. The wood has a light coating of some manner of varnish or slightly slick treatment, so it doesn't stick to the clay too badly, and keeps things fun to use. I like the bright primary colors in the natural wood tone, and the diverse shapes are a lot of fun. The only thing you should know is that a few of these are not entirely safe for extremely active toddlers, so this is a toy that you will supervise and make sure that nobody is sprinting down the hall with a small pointed spear. When used as directed and not as a weapon (mothers of small boys will understand my caveat), this is such a fun set!

I actually held one of them back, the rolling wheel that has little squares stamped into it, so my son can help me make peanut butter cookies by gently pushing the cookie with his roller. This one will remain food safe only, and the rest will be played with with modeling clays and play dough. I don't think these would be as fun and successful with more grown-up clays such as Fimo just because the surface area is so large and usually you are creating giant rough sculptures with an expensive material like Fimo or Sculpey. This is definitely the sort of thing you would use with children's modeling clay. A great starter set that would make a great auxiliary to a simple modeling dough gift.
text_fidelity_b: Alex Art Wooden Dough Tools Set Kids Art and Craft Activity

Mountains Out of Molehills | Family Board Game for 2-4 Players | Two-Level Gameboard Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Great Gateway Game for Ages 9+ This game hits that sweet spot where the complexity is enough for adults but not so high that kids struggle. And it’s FUN! It says 9 and up but my 7-year-old caught on pretty quickly and was delighted when we talked about it in terms of executing a program. My family loves this game. My husband and I can see playing it with just adults too.

The gameplay involves drafting cards and then using them to create a plan for how the mole will move on the grid, which is essentially a simple program much like one would write on a computer. It takes some strategy, but you can only predict other people so much and this is where the game shines.

I was worried it would be too complex or long when we read the rules, but it plays very smoothly! We felt comfortable within 2 rounds, and it was a lot of fun seeing how the plans we made would be thwarted as other players move. We also enjoyed how the turn order changed. There are many levels of subtle strategy, I feel like we will be learning new things each time we play. There is a random element of dice when placing a rock on the board, simple but genius game design. It keeps it from feeling unfair, and adds an element of luck to using it.

Even when you are losing, it’s so interesting to see the programs unfold as each card flips that it didn’t feel upsetting, and most of the points are earned in the later rounds as the mounds get higher so you can easily catch back up to an early lead or after a bad round. This means you don’t feel too discouraged if you have a poor start.

I like that it has a defined timeline, there are 6 rounds and you know what they will look like. Overall a great choice for a family game night as it is not likely to overrun an hour.

The double-layer boards and gameplay are unique and the story of the moles is full of flavor. The art is charming and the explanation of the rules such as “moles are too polite so they don’t move when they hit another” is a really sweet touch. The printing is great quality, the game is just beautiful to look at. The box is well-organized making setup and takedown easy, and it looks pretty on the shelf. Plus, we love the moles! The standees make great pieces. This game shows a lot of care in the details, and we love games with a lot of artistic flavor.

We play a lot of games as a family, but when we finished this one kiddo said this was their new favorite! The only downside is the limit of 2-4 players–it keeps it moving but means we can’t invite more friends to play at a time!

Bonus, the box art is beautiful so this also would make a lovely gift to open.
text_fidelity_b: Mountains Out of Molehills | Family Board Game for 2-4 Players | Two-Level Gameboard Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Great Gateway Game for Ages 9+

It was a good introduction to drone flying for me. I had planned on attaching a camera and expanding on my photography using this.

I will definitely need a bigger drone before I can do that but at least I was able to learn how to fly a drone since this is the first time I have ever had an experience with flying one.

The remote used to fly the drone however requires some AAA batteries, which did not come with it but you can get those just about anywhere. The control looks much like a video game controller so kids and teens who are already adept with holding a video game pad will be able to master this in no time.

The drone performed well on its intitial flight for me, and I even got it to do a few flips and rolls as well.

This is a decent little starter drone.

Seedling Design Your Own Virtual Reality Viewer: The Dark Side Activity Kit We are a technically competent family. Our experience as real users of this product was very underwhelming. The first step on their instructions is to download the Seedling app from their website, but we had to search their website for a good 20 minutes before we found the link to their app. The app is 128MB (for Android) which takes a good amount of time to download, as well as filling up a large amount of space on our phone.

While I'm waiting for the app to download, let me review the other parts of this package. What you're getting is essentially a basic Google Cardboard viewer (available separately for $5-$10 from various Amazon sellers) plus pieces of arts-and-crafts paper and plastic that you can glue to the cardboard viewer (a bottle of white glue is included). Maybe you can finish the glueing in about the time it takes for the 128MB app to download. There are no templates included in the directions and no photos of possible finished products (except for the 1 on the Amazon product description), but you're just glueing pieces of paper and plastic, so don't expect much.

Once you get the 128MB app downloaded and running, it asks you to download the Google Cardboard app, which is another 48MB. Download that and now you can play their maze game. There are a few pre-configured mazes and an apparent editor mode that lets you design your own maze. Designing your own maze is also discussed on the Amazon product description. I could not figure out how to get the maze editor to work in the app and the printed documentation included in the box is no help. Playing the pre-made mazes a couple of times gave me a headache, so designing my own maze doesn't sound very interesting anyway.

Now that I do have the Google Cardboard app on my phone, I'll probably just delete their maze app and try some of the Google Cardboard apps. I could have done that by just buying a $5 Google Cardboard instead of using this kit for $30. There really is nothing more to this product than their maze app, a Google Cardboard viewer, and some pieces of paper and plastic that you can cut up and glue to the Google Cardboard viewer. If your kids are into arts-and-crafts, they may get more out of that part of the product than I did. However, the arts-and-crafts has no association with the software and I don't see the point to mixing 2 unrelated projects. They should have put more work into their maze designer app. Maybe let you draw out mazes as the arts-and-crafts project and then scanning those into the software.
text_fidelity_b: Seedling Design Your Own Virtual Reality Viewer: The Dark Side Activity Kit

Magformers Magnets in Motion Set - Engineering Magnet Toys for Brain Development - 300 Pc Set I have bought three sets of magformers now for all of my grandchildren (3 to 14). Even toddlers can play with them because they are too large to swallow. They also like the solid shapes and colors of Magnatiles but those are more expensive. You can also get magnetic wooden blocks (Tegu) but those are really expensive so I haven't bought any.

The magformers are one of those toys that both kids and adults can sit and play with for an hour or longer. What I've noticed with three young grandkids together is that they each have their favorite pieces and styles of construction. One always creates vehicles, one creates houses, and the third makes towers. The colors and feel of the pieces are both soothing and exciting to work with.

Update: I had five kids and two adults playing with these recently and the person that seemed the most focused on building things is an MIT Neuroscientist. Once he built things following the guide, the kids quickly caught on and followed suit. I recommend that an adult work with the kids to begin with.

Regarding complaints about the magnets not working, if you snap together two piles of similarly shaped objects and then try to put the two piles together, sometimes the piles will reject each other. If you take one pile and start adding it to the other one at a time, all the pieces hold to each other. It seems as though the magnets must change polarity inside the plastic. I'd love a proper explanation.

I only recommend getting sets of 40 or more to have enough pieces to be creative. Wait for them to go on sale unless money is no object. Since all the grandkids took their sets home with them, I've bought a fourth set to keep at my house.

Addendum per request: I first chose these toys because of the brightly colored plastic material but soon discovered that having the pieces snap together and hold their shape is quite satisfying. While they don't take away from the joy of plain wooden blocks, they are different and allow you to vary how you play with them.

This particular kit is right for me because I'll have a crowd of five young children and many adults (thankfully two engineers) for two weeks over Christmas and I'll put this out on a large sofa table in the living room near the tree. That way the kids will feel like they have toys and waiting won't be so hard. It also incorporates many of the other kits you can buy separately so the kids can see specific types of builds.

Go to youtube and type in magformers to see how they are used. Construction is really that easy.
text_fidelity_b: Magformers Magnets in Motion Set - Engineering Magnet Toys for Brain Development - 300 Pc Set

A brush, pencil, tube of white, packet of 8 sheets of watercolor paper and a refillable brush pen are included. To refill the brush pen, twist it open in the opposite direction than you may anticipate. I recommend using distilled water for watercolors, it's not expensive and is available in most grocery stores.

This is a 48 color set of full pans. The variety is acceptable, but there is no color chart, colors are not labeled at all. The issue with this set is the pigments are weak, and the binder is very heaving making them all very opaque and chalky when dry. They blend okay, and blooming leaves much to be desired. The tin states it is compliant to ASTM D4236 and EN71. There is no way to verify this information. For this reason, I would be hesitant to recommend it for use by children.

I do not find the set to be a good value. There are other budget sets available in the same price range that prove to me much easier to use, with better pigment saturation. Thank you for reading my review. If it was Helpful to you, please kindly click the button below.

text_fidelity_a:
Electric Wiggle Car Ride On Toy, ANPABO 2 in 1 Wiggle Car with Rechargeable Battery and Pedal, Anti-Rollover Wheels with Colorful Lights, Swing Car for Toddlers and Kids Age 3 Years up Update: after a few months of off/on use- ours figured out how to ride on his own… don’t give up- kids can get the hang of it just fine!!!

Super excited in theory.. with ability to use manually or with electronic option as needed- it seemed ideal by just a flip of a switch on bottom. Only for some reason, pedal doesn’t respond every time like it should!! (Yes! battery is full when trying it- yet 15% of time it wont respond electronically- reason deducted x1 star!!?) When pedal engages- scooter is stable, easy to glide and maneuver.. and enjoyed. Battery outlasts our toddler whose rides for 15-25min straight and it hasn’t run out! (For reference: our little is 33mo, 36lb, 38” tall.. almost 3yr old.)

because of electronic component- ours struggles to grasp concept without using the pedal since he’s learned to ride with the electronic aid! So, when it fails to respond or we have pedal off- he just “jerks” scooter back/forth and side/side- its as if he’s trying to get it to do what it “should..” by tugging it into motion. For some reason.. he doesn’t naturally get moving scooter without electronic help so, it can leaves him fristrated.

Instructions are straightforward and connecting handle atop the scooter can be a tad tricky and tight.. Best if use included hardware to connect all screws loosely first THEN, tighten after all parts are aligned. Light up wheels are just extra!!! Not needed and not sure how long they’ll last esp. rider encountered water elements? I love the “long press” music feature- ha, it’s my fav. **bc, It shuts music all the way off!!

We’ve only used inside on tile and large smooth nape rug. No tire markings is nice.. I like inside option bc it’s winter here! I realize some issues had may be caused by our rider himself- but feel pedal should not be a problem we have to deal with if it’s charged. Hoping info can help decision.. stay safe everyone!
text_fidelity_b: Electric Wiggle Car Ride On Toy, ANPABO 2 in 1 Wiggle Car with Rechargeable Battery and Pedal, Anti-Rollover Wheels with Colorful Lights, Swing Car for Toddlers and Kids Age 3 Years up

text_fidelity_a: Kamigami Scarrax Robot - Discontinued by Manufacturer This box weighs next to nothing, and the contents are not particularly impressive when you open the box -- causing me to raise an eyebrow at what seems like a high price.  But after putting this toy together, you realize that you are not paying for the physical materials that make the toy, but rather for the programming that makes the toy fun.  In the box, you will find a flat plastic sheet stamped with eight parts, a bag of teeny-tinyplastic rivets for assembly, a USB charger cable, and some electronic body parts.  It takes a little bit of patience (and steady fingers) to put this the Scarrax together, but it is not particularly difficult, and no special tools are required.  It's mostly a matter of folding the pieces from the plastic sheet and snapping them together with the rivets.  I would allow an hour, at least, for getting everything together.  Once assembled, you can download the app on an apple or android device, and program your robot to do whatever.  Scarrax can really more -- you'd be surprised at his speed and dancing ability, particularly considering he's made from a single flat sheet of plastic.  I would say this is appropriate for late tweens and teens, although some younger children might be able to use it (1) if they're super geniuses or (2) with adult help.
text_fidelity_b: Kamigami Scarrax Robot - Discontinued by Manufacturer

That's my only complaint. The level is fun and you kinda have to buy it to unlock stuff on other level packs. You can choose which ghostbuster is in the game when you play, Egon, Ray, Peter or Winston.

Still better than that garbage they called a movie released recently. Much more fun to play the original than see a pile of... well... I digress.

text_fidelity_a: LEGO Friends Dolphins Rescue Mission 41378 Building Kit with Toy Submarine and Sea Creatures, Fun Sea Life Playset with Kacey and Stephanie Minifigures for Group Play (363 Pieces) Friends cartoon is a favorite, so this Lego set is a treat. As any Lego set, it comes with manual to put it together, lots of parts and fun time to put it together which can take anywhere from 1 to 3 hours depending on speed and you being interrupted. Then it's time to play! It's has enough to make up cute and adventurous scenarios to keep any girl occupied and creative. It's not called Friends for nothing. I recommend it.
